questions.q: What does the Box-Jenkins methodology prescribe as the three main steps for building an ARIMA-family model?
options: Forecast, backtest, deploy
Identify, estimate, diagnose
Difference, scale, normalize
Train, validate, test on separate neural networks
questions.explain: Box-Jenkins is the classical identify-estimate-diagnose loop: use ACF/PACF to suggest candidate orders, estimate the candidates, then check residual diagnostics before accepting the model.

questions.q: A series' PACF cuts off sharply after lag 2, while its ACF decays gradually. What does this pattern most strongly suggest?
options: A pure MA(2) process
A pure AR(2) process
The series is definitely non-stationary
A GARCH(1,1) process
questions.explain: A sharp PACF cutoff after lag p combined with a gradually decaying ACF is the classic signature of a pure AR(p) process — here, AR(2).

questions.q: Between AIC and BIC, which statement is correct?
options: AIC penalizes extra parameters more heavily than BIC and tends to prefer simpler models
BIC penalizes extra parameters more heavily than AIC and tends to prefer simpler models
AIC and BIC always select the identical model order
Lower AIC is worse, but lower BIC is better
questions.explain: BIC's complexity penalty grows with the log of the sample size and is generally heavier than AIC's, so BIC tends to favor more parsimonious models than AIC on the same data. Lower is better for both criteria.

questions.q: The Ljung-Box test on a fitted model's residuals returns a p-value of 0.01 at lag 10. What should you conclude?
options: The residuals are white noise and the model is adequately specified
The residuals show significant leftover autocorrelation, so the model is likely under-specified
The series is definitely stationary
The forecast will have zero error
questions.explain: The Ljung-Box null hypothesis is 'no autocorrelation in the residuals.' A small p-value (below the conventional 0.05 threshold) rejects that null, indicating leftover autocorrelation and an under-specified model.

questions.q: Why is it standard practice to fit several nearby (p, q) candidates rather than relying solely on an ACF/PACF plot to pick the exact order?
options: ACF and PACF plots are only usable for seasonal models
Real series' ACF/PACF often show gradual decay in both, without a clean cutoff, so plots suggest starting points rather than exact answers
AIC and BIC cannot be computed unless multiple models are fit
statsmodels requires fitting at least 16 models to converge
questions.explain: Mixed ARMA processes typically show gradual decay in both ACF and PACF with no clean cutoff, so the plots are used to narrow down a reasonable starting range, and AIC/BIC plus residual diagnostics decide among nearby candidates.
